target_customer: Adult readers of romance fiction who read on mobile, mostly via a free app with optional subscription
problem: Viral romance fiction from Kindle and BookTok authors was not available as short, visual comic episodes on a mobile app.
business_model: Freemium mobile content app with subscription and paid episodes
product_category: Consumer romance comics and visual series app using AI assisted production

founders.name: Fengjiao Peng
previous_startups: KURUKURU (earlier name of the product, a browser based 3D engine for comics)
founders.background_notes: Per the YC page: ML researcher at MIT Media Lab, engineer at Vimeo and Adobe, former comics creator. Education not stated.

technical_complexity.rationale: Comic production with generative AI plus a mobile reading app; the earlier KURUKURU product was a 3D engine for making comics, which was harder than the later content app.

defensibility.rationale: Content is licensed or adapted from authors and the app format is easy to copy; large webtoon platforms already served romance readers.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source found of an incumbent copying or buying Shortbread; the company remains listed as active.

market_need_then: Romance is a leading genre on webcomic platforms (per guides on Tapas and Manta) and BookTok drove demand for romance fiction. The app claims 100K downloads and 3,000 five star reviews (company claims).

branding.domain_note: Site is shortbread.ai; the earlier product used the name KURUKURU.

identity.visual_style: Illustrated romance comic art, 18 plus content
identity.voice_and_tone: Short, upbeat and direct, for example Read Spicy Romantic Comics

rebrands.why: YC page says KURUKURU is now Shortbread.ai; reason not stated

branding.community_and_virality: App claims to be the number one spicy romance reading app; no independent press or community evidence found.

brand_strength.rationale: A friendly food name that is easy to say, but shared with the biscuit and not tied to romance; no brand press found.

pivots.from: KURUKURU, a browser based 3D engine for creating comics
pivots.to: Shortbread, a consumer romance comics and series app
pivots.why: Not stated; YC page notes only that KURUKURU is now Shortbread.ai

outcome_analysis: Shortbread moved from a comics creation tool to a consumer romance content app and is still active with a very small team. The YC page credits the founder with about 500K dollars in revenue and 2 million episodes sold, which is a company claim. Funding is only visible on aggregators with conflicting figures, so its capital position and long term outcome are not established.
notes: Funding unverified and conflicting: CB Insights reports about $2.5M over four rounds including a $2M seed dated May 2023 (investors TSVC, Y Combinator, Pioneer Fund, Bat VC), while Extruct lists a $500K pre-seed in December 2022. No press release found, so no round recorded. The YC page text also lists two other people (Evan, Yiping Lyu) as founders without clear bios, while a search summary calls Fengjiao Peng the sole founder, so only she is listed. Education not found. No dated competitor sources found near the batch; Webtoon, Tapas and Radish are mentioned only in undated guides. Round update: the 2022-12 pre-seed rests on Extruct only and the 2023-05 seed on CB Insights only (listed under the legal name Kurukuru, about $2.5M over four rounds); the other rounds are not itemized and no press release confirms either.
